## Setup, global objects and dependencies

```{r}
#| label: packages

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
   DBI
  ,odbc
  ,dplyr
  ,dbplyr
  ,glue
  ,tidyverse
  ,gt
  ,ggplot2
  ,labelled
  ,sjlabelled
  ,hablar
  ,janitor
  ,scales
  )

pacman::p_load_gh("actepi/actepir")

# Attached non-base packages, for the dependency statement below.
#
# sessionInfo()$otherPkgs is a list of package descriptions carrying different
# numbers of fields depending on the package, so do.call(rbind, ...) recycles
# and warns. Reading the two fields we actually want avoids both the warning
# and a slow installed.packages() scan of the whole library tree.
pkgs <- utils::sessionInfo()$otherPkgs
packageslist <- if (length(pkgs)) {
  sort(vapply(pkgs, function(p) paste0(p$Package, " (", p$Version, ")"), character(1)))
} else {
  character(0)
}

rm(pkgs)
```

<!-- BEGIN:conn -->
### Connection

```{r}
#| label: conn121

con121 <- DBI::dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  Driver = "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server",
  Server = "PRDSQL121vs.act.gov.au",
  Trusted_Connection = "Yes",
  Port = 1433
  )

invisible(gc())   # retain to clear sporadic Type 29 ODBC error
```

<!-- END:conn -->
<!-- BEGIN:sel -->
### Data

Aliasing the remote table in its own chunk means the object exists in the
session as soon as the chunk runs, so RStudio can offer column names as
predictive text while the selection below is being written.

```{r}
#| label: lazy_alias

con121_tbl <- episerver_lazytable(con121, "ACTGHSMYX")
```

```{r}
#| label: selection

dt <- con121_tbl |>
  # filter() and select() narrow the query before it runs - everything stays
  # lazy until collect_withlabels() is reached
  # filter(SVYYEAR >= 2020) |>
  select(SVYYEAR, MY_SEX, AGE) |>
  collect_withlabels()
```

<!-- END:sel -->
<!-- BEGIN:sql -->
### Data (SQL)

An alternative to the dbplyr route. Results are written to `dt_sql` rather than
`dt`, so both approaches can sit in the document while you decide which suits
the job.

Note the `--|` option prefix: chunk options follow the comment syntax of the
chunk's own engine, so SQL uses `--|` where R uses `#|`.

```{sql}
--| label: selection-sql
--| connection: con121
--| output.var: dt_sql

SELECT TOP 100
       SVYYEAR, MY_SEX, AGE
FROM   Analysis.dbo.ACTGHSMYX
```

<!-- END:sql -->

```{=html}
<script>
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Workaround for a Quarto 1.8.x bug in the code-tools "Code" menu.
//
// Quarto's code-copy feature wraps each folded block's .sourceCode in
// <div class="code-copy-outer-scaffold">, but the built-in Show All / Hide All
// Code handler selects `.cell > details > .sourceCode` - a *direct* child - so
// it now matches nothing and the two menu items do nothing. (View Source uses a
// separate mechanism and is unaffected.) This re-binds the two items with a
// selector that matches the actual DOM. Harmless once Quarto fixes it upstream;
// remove then.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  function toggleAllCode(open) {
    document.querySelectorAll("details.code-fold").forEach(function (d) {
      if (open) { d.setAttribute("open", ""); } else { d.removeAttribute("open"); }
    });
    document.querySelectorAll(".cell > .sourceCode").forEach(function (c) {
      c.classList.toggle("hidden", !open);
      c.classList.toggle("unhidden", open);
    });
    return false;
  }
  var show = document.getElementById("quarto-show-all-code");
  var hide = document.getElementById("quarto-hide-all-code");
  if (show) { show.addEventListener("click", function () { return toggleAllCode(true); }); }
  if (hide) { hide.addEventListener("click", function () { return toggleAllCode(false); }); }
});
</script>
```
